claims.text: The modeled HfNbTaTiZr alloy is equimolar and as-annealed.
As-annealed HfNbTaTiZr possesses inherent chemical short-range order.
The initial alloy state is free of extrinsic defects.
Hybrid MC/MD can evolve realistic atomic-scale chemical disorder and short-range order for HfNbTaTiZr.
MD-derived phonon density-of-states calculations can extract the relevant lattice dynamics after MC/MD equilibration.
Local chemical short-range order and mass or force-constant fluctuations modulate the phonon density of states.
Realistic chemical disorder and short-range order alter the phonon energy landscape and phonon-scattering mechanisms.
MD-PDOS analysis decouples the lattice thermal-conductivity contribution from the electronic contribution.
The proposed MC/MD-PDOS workflow directly calculates lattice thermal transport.
The proposed approach will match experimental lattice thermal conductivity more closely than earlier analytical models.
The proposed approach will improve predictive accuracy by approximately 50% relative to earlier analytical models.
The predicted lattice-conductivity trend will be distinct from experimentally measured total conductivity.
Earlier approaches assume perfect defect-free crystals, use Debye-temperature-based analytical formulas, omit realistic disorder, and fail to separate lattice and electronic transport.
Phonon scattering dominates thermal transport in HfNbTaTiZr from 300 to 1200 K.
Below 200 K, lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions may be comparable.
The method becomes less reliable below 200 K and in samples with high extrinsic-defect concentrations.
Strong electron-phonon coupling or high impurity levels can make lattice/electronic decoupling less clear.
Inelastic neutron scattering and TDTR can provide a decoupled experimental lattice thermal conductivity for comparison with the simulation.
Chemical short-range order can be quantified using atom-probe tomography or X-ray/neutron diffraction.
A deviation exceeding ±30% between measured and predicted lattice conductivity across the test range is designated as falsifying the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as having no extrinsic defects, whereas the conditions allow approximately 1 wt.% oxygen and require a defect distribution representative of real samples.

The core claim describes lattice transport as independent of and decoupled from electronic transport, but the boundary and uncertainty fields concede that this decoupling may fail at low temperature, high impurity content, or strong electron-phonon coupling.
